newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to unveil 3-year refinery plan - Pemex.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to unveil 3-year refinery plan - Pemex.

text.p: Mexico is preparing a three-year plan for new investment in refineries, director general of state oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) Adrian Lajous said on Monday.

The plan, to be presented soon before Pemex's board of directors, aims to continue a process of improving gasoline quantity and processing, he said at the inaugurating of three new units at its Tula refinery.

"In it the principal investment decisions in refining will be put before the board," he said. "It looks to accommodate the expected growth in demand and process a greater volume of heavy crude in Mexican refineries."
Mexico has been working to boost its gasoline production and turn a glut of heavy crude into more value-added products.
The country has been aiming to eliminate leaded gasoline sales by the year 2000, as part of a plan to reduce polluting emissions.

About 75 percent of Mexico's gasoline sales is of unleaded, and leaded fuel is increasingly difficult to find, Lajous said. Just five years ago unleaded gasoline comprised less than 20 percent of gasoline sold, he added.
The move to phase out leaded gasoline is part of preparation for new environmental regulations that will come into effect beginning January 1998.

"One of the leading causes of air pollution is the content of toxic substances, such as lead and sulphur, which are indispensable for most production," Mexican president Ernesto Zedillo Ponce said at the event.
Falling prices of heavy Maya crude have also spurred moves to better process the fuel to value-added products.
In addition to new hydrosulfuric, alkilation and isomerization units at Tula, Pemex has built and renovated 24 refinery units since 1992, Lajous said.
